subject.title: [Bug] Sandbox validateEnvVarValue base64 heuristic false-positives on legitimate long alphanumeric values

question: Should sandbox env sanitization only warn on structurally base64-shaped values when env var names look credential-sensitive, or should the current value-only warning coverage remain?
rationale: This is a sandbox credential-warning policy tradeoff, not a purely mechanical false-positive cleanup.

options.title: Approve narrowed key-aware warning
options.body: Refresh the open PR and accept reduced warnings for neutral env names in exchange for fewer false positives.

options.title: Keep broader warning coverage
options.body: Leave the issue open or close the candidate PR if maintainers prefer warning on suspicious value shape regardless of key name.

options.title: Broaden the sensitive-name contract first
options.body: Expand the credential-name matcher before narrowing the value heuristic if maintainers want less false-positive noise without losing as much coverage.

recommendation.title: Approve narrowed key-aware warning
recommendation.body: Refresh the open PR and accept reduced warnings for neutral env names in exchange for fewer false positives.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the sanitizer behavior and is the strongest history-backed individual routing candidate for the security policy choice.
